title: AREA: Attribute Extraction and Aggregation for CLIP-Based Class-Incremental Learning
claim: Frozen encoders feed attribute extraction, task-specific expert aggregation with regularization, and transport-based routing, forming one end-to-end incremental-learning procedure.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right data flow, dashed zoom-in box for VIB
description: A wide single-panel diagram reading left to right. At far left, an MLLM icon and a query box generate captions for a real animal photo and for augmented versions (masked, flipped), shown as beige answer boxes with arrows. Image and text inputs pass through snowflake-marked frozen Visual and Textual Encoders. Each encoder feeds a 'Task-specific Residual Refinement' block, drawn as a gray rounded box inside a colored panel (green for visual, peach for text) containing task-specific scorers and small 3D bar charts. A hypersphere sketch labeled 'PGA-based Extraction' sits in the middle. Colored feature tiles joined by a contrastive loss link the two branches. A dashed zoom-in box shows VIB optimization with monotonous and invariant score bars. At right, a score vector and an optimal-transport plot with Sinkhorn cost and task attributes produce the prediction.
caption: Overview of \momo. We freeze CLIP throughout training. For each incoming task, we build multi-modal class attributes on the hypersphere via PGA from visual features and caption-augmented text embeddings. Then we train a lightweight task expert that aggregates anchored attributes using scoring and residual refinement, regularized with a variational information bottleneck objective. At inference time, we use Sinkhorn optimal-transport routing over task attribute manifolds and softly combine the experts’ predictions.
abstract: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) is important in building real-world learning systems. In CLIP-based CIL, the model performs classification by comparing similarity between visual and textual embeddings obtained from template prompts, e.g., ``a photo of a [CLASS]''. This seemingly monolithic matching process can be decomposed into two conceptually distinct stages: attribute extraction and attribute aggregation. For example, a model may recognize cat using attributes such as fur texture and whiskers. When learning a new class like car, the model must extract additional attributes like wheels and adjust how they are aggregated in the shared representation space. However, since only data from the current task is available, incremental updates can bias both attribute extraction and aggregation toward new classes, leading to catastrophic forgetting. Therefore, we propose AREA for attribute extraction and aggregation in CLIP-based CIL. To stabilize extraction, we anchor class-level visual and textual attributes on the hyperspherical embedding space via principal geodesic analysis. To stabilize aggregation, we learn lightweight task-specific experts with scoring and residual refinement, regularized by a variational information bottleneck objective. During inference, we perform routing over task attribute manifolds via optimal transport for more concise prediction. Experiments show that AREA consistently outperforms SOTA methods. Code is available at https://github.com/LAMDA-CL/ICML2026-AREA.
